chapter.en: PART I PRELIMINARY

text.en: 1. These Regulations may be cited as the Casino Control (Credit) Regulations 2010 and shall come into operation on 3rd February 2010.

chapter.en: PART I PRELIMINARY
PART IA DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS AND MODES OF PAYMENT FOR CASINO GAMBLING
PART IA DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS AND MODES OF PAYMENT FOR CASINO GAMBLING

text.en:
2B. A casino operator may establish for a patron of the casino of that casino operator a deposit account to which is to be credited the amount representing any deposit of money or other permitted deposit to the account.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IA DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS AND MODES OF PAYMENT FOR CASINO GAMBLING

heading.en: Issue of chip purchase vouchers, etc., and debit to deposit account

text.en:
2C. A casino operator may issue to a patron and debit to the patron’s deposit account chip purchase vouchers, cheques, casino chips or money, not exceeding in total value the credit balance in the account at the time of issue of the vouchers, cheques, casino chips or money.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IA DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS AND MODES OF PAYMENT FOR CASINO GAMBLING

heading.en: Issue of chip purchase vouchers in exchange for cheque or traveller’s cheque

text.en:
2D. A casino operator may, in exchange for a cheque payable to the casino operator or traveller’s cheque, issue to a patron chip purchase vouchers of a value equivalent to the amount of the cheque or traveller’s cheque.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IA DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS AND MODES OF PAYMENT FOR CASINO GAMBLING

heading.en: Deposit of cheque accepted by casino operator

text.en:
2E. If a casino operator accepts a cheque payable to the casino operator or a traveller’s cheque —
(a)for the purpose of crediting the amount representing that cheque to a deposit account under regulation 2B; or
(b)in exchange for the issue of chip purchase vouchers under regulation 2D,
the casino operator —
(c)must deposit with an authorised bank the cheque or traveller’s cheque within 5 days after the date it is accepted; and
(d)must not agree to the redemption of the cheque or traveller’s cheque mentioned in paragraph (c) for the purpose of avoiding compliance with that paragraph.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II PERMITTED AND PROHIBITED TRANSACTIONS RELATING TO CREDIT

text.en:
5.—(1) For the purposes of section 108(1) of the Act, a casino operator may carry out the following transactions with a patron who is a person mentioned in section 108(7)(a) or (b) of the Act:
(a)accept payment for casino chips by charging to the patron’s credit card;
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)provide a cheque-cashing facility to the patron;
(c)allow to be credited to the patron’s deposit account the amount of a cheque payable to the casino operator before the cheque has been deposited with and cleared by an authorised bank;
(d)where the patron is a person referred to in section 108(7)(a) of the Act, provide an amount on credit to the patron which is to be credited to the patron’s deposit account for the purpose of qualifying him as a premium player of its casino.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) For the purposes of section 108(1) of the Act, a licensed international market agent may provide an amount on credit to a person mentioned in section 108(8) of the Act which is to be credited to the person’s deposit account with a casino operator for the purpose of qualifying him as a premium player of its casino.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II PERMITTED AND PROHIBITED TRANSACTIONS RELATING TO CREDIT

heading.en: Credit qualifying programme for premium player who is either a citizen of Singapore or a permanent resident of Singapore

text.en:
5A.—(1) A casino operator may, on or after 30th April 2013, provide credit to a premium player who is either a citizen of Singapore or a permanent resident of Singapore only in accordance with all of the following requirements relating to credit:
(a)the premium player to be provided credit by the casino operator must first register for a credit qualifying programme with the casino operator with respect to its casino and qualify for credit under that programme;
(b)the casino operator must be satisfied of that premium player’s creditworthiness based on its credit policy, procedures and controls referred to in regulation 12; and
(c)the premium player has drawn down and utilised for casino gambling from his deposit account with the casino operator a sum of money (referred to in this regulation as the principal capital) of at least $100,000 before he is provided any credit.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Where a premium player who is either a citizen of Singapore or a permanent resident of Singapore is registered for a credit qualifying programme with a casino operator with respect to its casino, the casino operator shall not, except with reasonable excuse, regard any winnings by that premium player from any casino gambling in determining the principal capital for the purposes of paragraph (1)(c).
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) Where a premium player who is either a citizen of Singapore or a permanent resident of Singapore qualifies for credit under a casino operator’s credit qualifying programme, and he does not cease to qualify as a premium player under regulation 3C(6) or regulation 4(5) (as in force immediately before 21 September 2026), for the remainder of the period that he is a premium player —
(a)he remains qualified for credit with that casino operator; and
(b)he does not have to re-register for a credit qualifying programme with the casino operator or re-qualify for credit under that programme.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a premium player who is either a citizen of Singapore or a permanent resident of Singapore may continue to be provided credit by a casino operator under any credit agreement entered into between that premium player and the casino operator before and subsisting on 30th April 2013 until the expiry or termination of the credit agreement provided that no amendment is made to the validity period or the maximum credit limit under the credit agreement.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II PERMITTED AND PROHIBITED TRANSACTIONS RELATING TO CREDIT

heading.en: Use of credit by licensed international market agent, etc.

text.en:
5B. A licensed international market agent, an associate of a licensed international market agent or a licensed international market agent representative must not use any credit provided by a casino operator under section 108(7)(c) of the Act for the purposes of casino gambling on his or her own account, unless he or she complies with all the requirements relating to credit applicable to him or her as a patron under the Act, these Regulations, the Casino Control (Casino Marketing Arrangements) Regulations 2013 and the Casino Control (Internal Controls) Regulations 2013 (G.N. No. S 59/2013).
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II PERMITTED AND PROHIBITED TRANSACTIONS RELATING TO CREDIT

heading.en: No provision of credit without prior request

text.en:
6. A casino operator or a licensed international market agent shall not —
(a)provide any credit to a patron except on the prior request of the patron; or
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)provide a higher amount of credit to a patron than the amount of credit requested by the patron.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II PERMITTED AND PROHIBITED TRANSACTIONS RELATING TO CREDIT
PART III ESTABLISHING AND MAINTAINING CREDIT ACCOUNT AND CHEQUE-CASHING ACCOUNT

text.en:
8.—(1) Any casino operator wishing to provide any credit to a patron shall establish for that patron —
(a)a credit account through which may be provided credit for a deposit account; or
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)a cheque-cashing account through which may be granted a cheque-cashing facility,
or both, and shall comply with the requirements in this Part in relation to the account or accounts.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Any licensed international market agent wishing to provide any credit to a patron shall establish for that patron a credit account, through which may be provided credit for a deposit account, and shall comply with the requirements in this Part in relation to the account.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART III ESTABLISHING AND MAINTAINING CREDIT ACCOUNT AND CHEQUE-CASHING ACCOUNT

text.en:
9.—(1) A casino operator or a licensed international market agent shall, before establishing a credit account for a patron under regulation 8, enter into a credit agreement in accordance with paragraph (2) with the patron.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(2) The credit agreement to be entered into with the patron shall be in writing and be signed by the parties or their authorised representatives, and shall contain all the terms and conditions governing the provision of credit to the patron, including the following:
(a)the names of the parties to the credit agreement;
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(b)the nationality of the patron;
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(c)the countries in which the patron has been granted permanent residency;
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(d)the terms and conditions relating to the provision of credit to a patron when the patron becomes a citizen of Singapore or permanent resident of Singapore;
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(e)the date on which the credit agreement was entered into;
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(f)the validity period of the credit agreement;
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(g)the maximum credit limit of the patron under the credit agreement;
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(h)the patron’s eligibility to draw upon the full amount of credit provided under the credit agreement, up to the credit limit referred to in sub-paragraph (g); and
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(i)any interest or other consideration payable by the patron for the provision of credit to him.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART III ESTABLISHING AND MAINTAINING CREDIT ACCOUNT AND CHEQUE-CASHING ACCOUNT

text.en:
10.—(1) A casino operator may, upon an application by a patron for a cheque-cashing facility in accordance with paragraph (2), establish for the patron a cheque-cashing account through which may be granted a cheque-cashing facility.
(2) An application for a cheque-cashing facility shall be in writing and shall contain —
(a)the date on which the application is made;
(b)the name and signature of the patron making the application; and
(c)the name and signature of the person approving the application on behalf of the casino operator, and in respect of the approved cheque-cashing facility —
(i)the validity period of the cheque-cashing facility granted;
(ii)the maximum credit limit of the patron granted under the cheque-cashing facility; and
(iii)any interest or other consideration payable by the patron for the granting of the cheque-cashing facility to him.

chapter.en: PART III ESTABLISHING AND MAINTAINING CREDIT ACCOUNT AND CHEQUE-CASHING ACCOUNT

text.en:
11.—(1) Every casino operator and licensed international market agent shall keep, in relation to each patron of the casino to whom the casino operator or licensed international market agent provides credit, as the case may be —
(a)a copy of the credit agreement entered into with the patron and any supporting documentation, amendment or supplementary agreement thereto for not less than 5 years after the expiry of the agreement;
(b)a copy of any application for a cheque-cashing facility by the patron for not less than 5 years after the expiry of the facility; and
(c)the following records relating to the patron’s credit account and, where applicable, cheque-cashing account for not less than 5 years after the completion of the transaction to which the record relates:
(i)in the case of a casino operator, the records specified in any requirements under these Regulations or the Casino Control (Internal Controls) Regulations 2013 (G.N. No. S 59/2013) or any directions given by the Authority under any of those Regulations; and
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
(ii)in the case of a licensed international market agent —
(A)the amount of credit given for a patron’s deposit account, and the date of issue of that amount;
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(B)the amount of each repayment of credit given for the patron’s deposit account, and the date of such repayment; and
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(C)such other records specified in any requirements under these Regulations or the Casino Control (Internal Controls) Regulations 2013 or any directions given by the Authority under any of those Regulations.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) A casino operator or a licensed international market agent shall, whenever requested by the Authority to do so —
(a)produce to the Authority all records referred to in paragraph (1) and permit the examination of those records, the taking of extracts from them and the making copies of them; and
(b)furnish to the Authority all such information as the Authority may require in connection with any such records.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART III ESTABLISHING AND MAINTAINING CREDIT ACCOUNT AND CHEQUE-CASHING ACCOUNT

text.en:
12.—(1) Every casino operator and licensed international market agent shall, before providing any credit, develop and implement a credit policy and procedures and controls relating to the provision of credit to its patrons, and shall communicate these to its employees and officers.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The credit policy, procedures and controls referred to in paragraph (1) shall include —
(a)the credit assessment criteria by which the creditworthiness of a patron is to be assessed;
(b)the credit limits applicable to different classes of patrons;
(c)the approving authority and procedures for the approval of —
(i)the establishment of a credit account or cheque-cashing account for a patron; and
(ii)the patron’s credit limit and any increase in credit limit;
(d)the procedures for the issuance of credit and the administration of a credit account or cheque-cashing account;
(e)the records and documents to be kept and checks to be carried out in relation to a credit account or cheque-cashing account; and
(f)debt recovery procedures.
(3) Every casino operator and licensed international market agent shall ––
(a)cause its credit policy, procedures and controls to be reviewed at least once in every 6 months by an employee or employees holding a senior managerial or executive position of the casino operator or licensed international market agent, as the case may be;
(b)ensure that its credit policy, procedures and controls are implemented in all its branch offices, whether in Singapore or elsewhere; and
(c)produce its credit policy, procedures and controls to the Authority for inspection whenever requested to do so.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]

chapter.en: PART IV GENERAL

heading.en: Duties of licensed special employee in relation to credit

text.en:
13.—(1) A licensed special employee of a casino operator must not extend credit in any form to a patron of the casino other than on behalf of the casino operator and in accordance with the Act and these Regulations.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Any licensed special employee who contravenes paragraph (1) shall be liable to disciplinary action under section 93 of the Act.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IV GENERAL

heading.en: Power to take disciplinary action against casino operator and licensed international market agent, etc.

text.en:
14.—(1) Any casino operator which —
(a)wilfully, recklessly or negligently treats a patron as a premium player where the patron —
(i)is not qualified as a premium player under regulation 3B;
(ii)has not retained the patron’s qualification as a premium player under regulation 3C(1), (2), (4) or (5);
(iii)has ceased to be a premium player under regulation 3C(3) or (6); or
(iv)is disqualified under regulation 4(1);
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)[Deleted by S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)[Deleted by S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(d)[Deleted by S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(e)[Deleted by S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(f)provides credit to a premium player not in accordance with regulation 5A(1) and (2); or
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(g)[Deleted by S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(h)contravenes regulation 2E(c) or (d), 4(4), 5(1), 6, 8(1), 9(1), 10(1), 11 or 12,
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

(2) Any licensed international market agent who ––

[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IV GENERAL

text.en:
15.—(1) Any associate of a licensed international market agent who contravenes regulation 5B shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or to both.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Any patron, for the purpose of obtaining credit not in accordance with regulation 5A(1), falsely represents to any casino operator that he is not a citizen of Singapore or a permanent resident of Singapore, shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or to both.
[S 61/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

PART IB
PREMIUM PLAYER QUALIFICATION
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
Forms of deposit by premium player
3. For the purposes of paragraph (a) of the definition of “premium player” in section 2(1) of the Act, the following forms of deposit are prescribed:
(a)money received by the casino operator from the patron in the form of cash, a cashier’s order or a bank draft payable to the casino operator or an electronic funds transfer to the casino operator’s bank account;
(b)casino chips or a traveller’s cheque received by the casino operator from the patron;
(c)a casino cheque payable to the patron that is accepted by the casino operator;
(d)a cheque payable to the casino operator that is issued by the patron and has been deposited with and cleared by an authorised bank;
(e)where the patron is neither a citizen nor permanent resident of Singapore, an amount on credit provided by the casino operator or a licensed international market agent to the patron under section 108(7) or (8) of the Act.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
Period of credit balance to remain premium player
3A. For the purposes of paragraph (b) of the definition of “premium player” in section 2(1) of the Act, the prescribed period is a continuous period of 12 months.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
When patron first qualifies as premium player
3B. A patron of a casino first qualifies as a premium player of the casino when the casino operator of that casino establishes a deposit account for the patron and the patron makes a deposit to that account in accordance with regulation 3 that results in the minimum balance being met in that account.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
When patron remains or ceases to be premium player
3C.—(1) After a patron of a casino first qualifies as a premium player of the casino in accordance with regulation 3B, the patron remains a premium player of that casino for 12 months starting on the date the patron so qualifies, unless otherwise expressly provided in this regulation.
(2) Where the credit balance in the deposit account of a patron who is a premium player of a casino falls below the minimum balance, the patron remains a premium player of that casino if —
(a)the period during which the credit balance in that account is less than the minimum balance does not exceed the period mentioned in regulation 3A; and
(b)during that period, one or more deposits in accordance with regulation 3 are made to that account which results in the minimum balance being met in that account.
(3) A patron of a casino who qualified as a premium player of that casino when the patron was neither a citizen nor permanent resident of Singapore ceases to be a premium player when the patron becomes a citizen or permanent resident of Singapore, unless the patron remains a premium player under paragraph (4).
(4) If, upon becoming a citizen or permanent resident of Singapore, the patron makes a deposit to the patron’s deposit account in accordance with regulation 3 which results in the minimum balance being met in that account, the patron remains a premium player of the casino for 12 months starting on the date the patron makes the deposit.
(5) Where the credit balance in the deposit account of a patron who is a premium player of a casino meets the minimum balance on —
(a)the next anniversary of the date mentioned in paragraph (1) (if applicable to the patron);
(b)the next anniversary of the date on which the deposit mentioned in paragraph (2)(b) or (4) is made (if applicable to the patron); or
(c)the date immediately after the end of the further period referred to in this paragraph (if applicable to the patron),
that patron remains a premium player of that casino for a further period of 12 months starting on that date.
(6) A patron ceases to be a premium player of a casino when the patron’s deposit account with the casino operator is closed or the patron does not retain the patron’s qualification as a premium player under paragraph (1), (2), (4) or (5), whichever is earlier.
(7) Nothing in this regulation prevents a patron who is a premium player of a casino from applying to close the patron’s deposit account with the casino operator.
Illustration 1
Patron A makes a deposit of $100,000 to Patron A’s deposit account with a casino operator on 2 January 2027. Patron A qualifies as a premium player of the casino operator’s casino on 2 January 2027. Patron A draws down $100,000 from that account on 4 January 2027 to participate in casino gambling at the casino operator’s casino. On 4 January 2027, the credit balance in that account is recorded as $0. Patron A continues to retain Patron A’s qualification as a premium player, which will cease on 1 January 2028 or when that account is closed, whichever is earlier.
Illustration 2
Patron B makes a deposit of $100,000 to Patron B’s deposit account with a casino operator on 2 January 2027. Patron B qualifies as a premium player of the casino operator’s casino on 2 January 2027. Patron B draws down $20,000 from that account on 4 January 2027 to participate in casino gambling at the casino operator’s casino. On 4 January 2027, the credit balance in that account is recorded as $80,000. Patron B makes a further deposit of $30,000 to that account on 6 January 2027, which results in a credit balance of $110,000 in that account. Patron B re-qualifies as a premium player on 6 January 2027. Patron B’s qualification as a premium player will cease on 5 January 2028 or when that account is closed, whichever is earlier.
Illustration 3
Patron B does not carry out further transactions in respect of Patron B’s deposit account after 6 January 2027. The credit balance in that account remains at $110,000 on 5 January 2028. Patron B does not close that account on 6 January 2028. As of 6 January 2028, the credit balance in that account is $110,000. Patron B remains a premium player on 6 January 2028 without having to make a further deposit of $100,000.
Note: Patron B in Illustration 3 is the same Patron B in Illustration 2.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
Disqualification of patron as premium player
4.—(1) A patron (X) who is a premium player of a casino (whether X qualified as a premium player before, on or after 21 September 2026) is disqualified as a premium player of that casino if X uses a round-tripping arrangement described in paragraph (2) with another patron (Y) to make a deposit of at least $10,000 to X’s deposit account with the casino operator of that casino.
(2) The round-tripping arrangement mentioned in paragraph (1) is as follows:
(a)the credit balance in X’s deposit account —
(i)immediately before X made the deposit of at least $10,000, was less than the minimum balance; and
(ii)immediately after X made that deposit, meets the minimum balance;
(b)before X made that deposit, Y who was a premium player of the casino withdrew money comprising the amount of the deposit from Y’s deposit account with the casino operator of the casino and gave the money to X;
(c)immediately after Y withdrew the money, the credit balance in Y’s deposit account was less than the minimum balance;
(d)the aggregate amount of the wagers made by Y participating in casino gambling in the casino during the period —
(i)starting on the date when Y last qualified, or remained qualified, as a premium player under regulation 3B or 3C(1), (2), (4) or (5), or regulation 3 or 4(1), (2), (3) or (4) (as in force immediately before 21 September 2026); and
(ii)ending at the time Y gave the money to X,
was less than 90% of the amount of the money given by Y to X.
(3) The disqualification mentioned in paragraph (1) takes effect at the time when the patron (X) makes the deposit mentioned in that paragraph.
(4) The casino operator must close the deposit account of a patron who is disqualified as a premium player of the casino under paragraph (1).
(5) To avoid doubt, paragraph (4) does not stop —
(a)the casino operator from establishing another deposit account for the patron under regulation 2B; or
(b)the patron from qualifying again as a premium player of that casino under regulation 3B,
after the patron’s deposit account has been closed in accordance with paragraph (4).
(6) Where any credit is provided by a casino operator to a patron who has been disqualified as a premium player of the casino under paragraph (1) after the patron is so disqualified and (if applicable) before the patron qualifies again as a premium player of that casino under regulation 3B, the amount of credit provided is recoverable by the casino operator as a debt due to the casino operator.
[S 636/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
